subject: general
question: Which glands help in digestion in the stomach?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gastric glands**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gastric glands** are responsible for aiding digestion in the stomach.
 
• These glands secrete gastric juice, which contains hydrochloric acid and digestive enzymes such as pepsin.
 
• The hydrochloric acid creates an acidic environment that helps in breaking down food, and the enzyme pepsin breaks down proteins into peptides.
 
• Gastric glands are located in the lining of the stomach and play a crucial role in the digestive process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gastric glands** are composed of different types of cells, including parietal cells, chief cells, and mucous cells.
 
• **Parietal cells** secrete hydrochloric acid, which helps in killing bacteria and activating pepsinogen to pepsin.
 
• **Chief cells** produce pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of pepsin.
 
• **Mucous cells** secrete mucus to protect the stomach lining from the harsh acidic environment.
 
• Malfunction or diseases affecting the gastric glands can lead to digestive issues such as ulcers and gastritis.
